summary: The Brownfields Reauthorization Act of 2025 extends and modifies the Environmental Protection Agency's Brownfields Program through fiscal year 2030. It increases maximum grant amounts for site cleanup, expands entity eligibility to include certain non-profit organizations and Alaska Native corporations, reduces or waives matching fund requirements for small and disadvantaged communities, authorizes appropriations for state response programs, and requires reporting to streamline the grant application process.

affected_groups.effect: Gain eligibility to apply for and receive Brownfields Program resources.
affected_groups.group: Tax-exempt 501(c)(6) organizations and Alaska Native Corporations

affected_groups.effect: Receive a complete waiver of the cost-sharing matching requirement for grants and targeted strategies to incentivize their applications.
Face a reduced cost-sharing requirement of 10% instead of 20%, can receive up to $1 million per site for remediation, and no longer face a 5% cap on administrative cost usage.
Authorized to receive specific annual appropriations ranging from $50 million to $75 million through 2030 to implement response programs.

key_provisions: Extends authorization for the Brownfields Program through fiscal year 2030.
Expands grant eligibility to tax-exempt 501(c)(6) organizations (such as chambers of commerce) and Alaska Native Regional and Village Corporations.
Increases the maximum remediation grant amount per site to $1,000,000.
Reduces the cost-sharing matching requirement for grant recipients from 20% to 10%, and requires the EPA to waive matching requirements entirely for small communities or disadvantaged areas.
Authorizes specific yearly appropriations for state and Indian tribe response programs ranging from $50,000,000 in fiscal year 2025 to $75,000,000 in fiscal year 2030.
Requires grant applicants to have a plan for engaging and involving a diverse set of local groups and community organizations directly affected by the project.
Directs the EPA to submit a report to Congress evaluating application criteria and to update guidance to streamline the application process within one year.
missing_information: Specific details on the exact total overall authorization amounts for the general Brownfields Program beyond the state response program appropriations lines are not fully detailed in the provided text excerpts outside of extending the timeframe through 2030.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Brownfields Reauthorization Act of 2025 extends and modifies the Environmental Protection Agency's Brownfields Program through fiscal year 2030. It increases maximum grant amounts for site cleanup, expands entity eligibility to include certain non-profit organizations and Alaska Native corporations, reduces or waives matching fund requirements for small and disadvantaged communities, authorizes appropriations for state response programs, and requires reporting to streamline the grant application process.
summary_detail.significance: The bill reauthorizes and funds federal environmental cleanup programs for contaminated properties through 2030, alters financial matching rules to assist disadvantaged areas, and broadens the types of organizations permitted to receive federal remediation grants.
